_note: The fixture's declared fictions, with a reason per line. The stand-in model writes each summary from the case's own values and then applies these rates; the reviewer model scores fluency and completeness with noise and flags a bad claim only sometimes. Nothing here is a measurement of any real model or reviewer; ADR-005 says which claims need the real thing.

v1.reason: the active version: terse instructions, omits a detail often, invents little; the baseline every candidate is measured against

v2.reason: the rewrite everyone wants to ship: reads better and omits less, and invents more; its review score rises by less than the thirty-review floor and its bad-claim count rises by more than the two-hundred-case floor

v3.reason: the careful rewrite with the retriever and the Apex provider: invents least from nothing and quotes the retrieved chunk half the time, which is the mis-grounding source when the retriever brought the wrong product

invented_sentences.reason: the sentences the stand-in invents; each carries an identifier and a date the case never had, so the grammar grades it unsupported
templates: A replacement unit was shipped under RMA-{rma} on {date}.
Invoice INV-{inv} was issued on {date} for the repair.
The customer was told a firmware update would arrive on {date}.

contradictions.reason: which atom a contradiction displaces and how; priority, status, amount and contact have field counterparts and grade contradicted, a date has none and grades unsupported

reviewers.reason: three reviewers score fluency and completeness with independent noise; one is harsher by a constant; a bad claim is flagged with a probability well below one, so the blind-spot count and the flag rate cannot contradict each other

retrieval.reason: three chunks per case: two from the case's product and one general, except in a quarter of cases where one chunk is for another product, which is what a retriever over a shared index does
